Actions on Objectives
—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] CodeIgniter4 framework fingerprinting in HTTP response (vulnerable-version recon) · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Polyglot upload: image magic bytes + PHP code in file written to webroot (CVE-2026-48062 payload) · [LLM] Multipart upload: filename extension mismatches declared Content-Type (ext_in bypass attempt)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] HTTP GET to PHP file inside /uploads path (CodeIgniter4 webshell invocation) · [LLM] Upload immediately followed by web-server shell execution (CVE-2026-48062 RCE chain)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
CodeIgniter4 framework fingerprinting in HTTP response (vulnerable-version recon) AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunts for HTTP responses that betray a CodeIgniter4 backend (X-Powered-By header, debug-toolbar markers, /index.php/controller/method route shape). Identifies attacker recon against potentially vulnerable CVE-2026-48062 instances before the upload bypass is attempted. Rationale: Article identifies CodeIgniter4 (composer:codeigniter4/framework < 4.7.2) as the affected product. The framework's canonical front-controller route is /index.php/controller/method and the bundled debug toolbar exposes _debugbar/ci_session markers — attackers fingerprint these before targeting CVE-2026-48062. Cross-checked against: • https://codeigniter.com/user_guide/incoming/routing.html • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx
ATT&CKT1592.002 T1595.002
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate users browsing CodeIgniter-built admin portals with /index.php/ routes
  • Internal QA scanners (Burp, ZAP) probing dev/staging CodeIgniter apps
  • SEO crawlers indexing /index.php routes
  • Authorized pentest engagements using nuclei/sqlmap against the app
Suppression filter
| where csUserAgent !has_any ("Googlebot", "bingbot", "YandexBot")
| where cIP !in ("<internal-vuln-scanner-IPs>")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Correlate the source IPs against threat-intel feeds and check whether they hit only /index.php-style URLs vs. natural browsing. Pull the cIP's full session — natural users follow links; scanners enumerate. Step 2 (contain): If clearly hostile (scanner UA + high path-diversity), block the cIP at WAF/edge and confirm the CodeIgniter4 instance is patched to >= 4.7.3. If not patched, prioritize emergency upgrade and disable any avatar/upload endpoints exposed publicly. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the same cIP/UA across all webservers for the last 30 days for upload POSTs to multipart/form-data endpoints; cross-check DeviceFileEvents for any .php drops in webroot.
// Defender XDR does not surface inbound HTTP response bodies/headers; recon is best hunted on web-tier telemetry shipped to Sentinel/Splunk.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe", "httpd.exe", "nginx.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "php-fpm")
| summarize Hits = count(), distinctSrc = dcount(RemoteIP) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where distinctSrc >= 5
| order by Timestamp desc
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)/index\.php(/|$)"
   or csUriQuery has_any ("_debugbar", "ci_session", "CI_VFS")
   or csUserAgent has_any ("sqlmap", "nuclei", "nmap", "acunetix", "wpscan")
| summarize HitCount = count(), Paths = make_set(csUriStem, 20), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
          by Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csUserAgent
| where HitCount >= 5
| order by LastSeen desc
title: CodeIgniter4 Application Fingerprinting via /index.php Route Probing
id: 5e0c1c0a-3a76-4cd2-9b1a-6f3c14c0e3d2
description: Detects HTTP requests matching the CodeIgniter4 /index.php/controller/method route shape and debug-toolbar artifacts, indicative of recon against CVE-2026-48062-vulnerable hosts.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.reconnaissance
  - attack.t1592.002
  - attack.t1595.002
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection_route:
    cs-uri-stem|re: '(?i)/index\.php(/|$)'
  selection_artifacts:
    cs-uri-query|contains:
      - '_debugbar'
      - 'ci_session'
  selection_scanner_ua:
    cs(User-Agent)|contains:
      - 'sqlmap'
      - 'nuclei'
      - 'nmap'
      - 'acunetix'
  condition: selection_route or selection_artifacts or selection_scanner_ua
level: low
source:(nginx OR apache OR iis) (@http.url_details.path:*/index.php/* OR @http.url_details.queryString:*_debugbar* OR @http.url_details.queryString:*ci_session*)
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.http_user_agent) as agents from datamodel=Web where Web.url="*/index.php/*" OR Web.http_method="GET" by Web.src Web.dest Web.status | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | search urls="*/index.php/*" OR urls="*?_debugbar*" OR urls="*/ci_session*" | where count >= 5
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.http_user_agent) as agents from datamodel=Web where Web.url="*/index.php/*" OR Web.http_method="GET" by Web.src Web.dest Web.status | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | search urls="*/index.php/*" OR urls="*?_debugbar*" OR urls="*/ci_session*" | where count >= 5
Polyglot upload: image magic bytes + PHP code in file written to webroot (CVE-2026-48062 payload) AIDelivery High
Hunts new files written to public web directories that combine an image-format magic header (GIF87a/GIF89a/JFIF/PNG) with embedded PHP markers (<?php, eval, system, passthru). This is the exact masquerading shape the article describes ('shell.php containing GIF-like content') that bypasses CodeIgniter4's ext_in validation. Rationale: Article: 'an uploaded file named shell.php containing GIF-like content could pass validation ... save uploaded files using the original client filename: $file->move($path), store uploads in a web-accessible directory'. Filtering on web-server parent process writing .php into upload/public/writable/avatar paths catches the exact CVE-2026-48062 payload drop. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/File_Upload_Cheat_Sheet.html • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html
ATT&CKT1036.008 T1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate CMS plugin install writing .php to a public path
  • CI/CD deploy of a PHP app extracting files into webroot via the web-server account
  • Composer/artisan operations triggered through a web interface
  • Developer staging environment with hot-reload of .php under /public
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("composer", "artisan", "wp-cli", "deploy.sh")
| where FolderPath !has_any ("\\vendor\\", "\\node_modules\\", "\\.git\\")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the file SHA256, the InitiatingProcessCommandLine, and the upstream HTTP request that ID'd the upload (correlate by Timestamp ± 5s on the same DeviceName). Inspect first 16 bytes — GIF87a/89a/FFD8FF/89504E47 followed by <?php is a confirmed polyglot. Step 2 (contain): Quarantine the file, kill any spawned worker processes that loaded it, isolate the host pending forensic image, and disable the upload endpoint (or hot-patch CodeIgniter4 to >= 4.7.3). Block the source IP at WAF. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep every public webroot in the estate for newly-written .php/.phtml/.phar in the last 30 days; pivot on the source IP across W3CIISLog for additional upload POSTs; check for crontab/Run-key persistence or outbound C2 from the web-server account.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed", "FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe", "httpd.exe", "nginx.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "php-fpm", "caddy.exe")
| where FileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php[3457]?|phtml|phar|pht|inc)$"
| where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)(\\|/)(uploads?|public|writable|avatar|images?|media|assets)(\\|/)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, RequestSourceIP, RequestAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(w3wp|httpd|nginx|php-cgi|php-fpm|caddy)(\.exe)?$"
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("php", "phtml", "phar", "php3", "php5", "php7", "pht", "inc")
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)(\\|/)(uploads?|public|writable|avatar|images?|media|assets)(\\|/)"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: PHP File Written to Web-Accessible Upload Directory by Web Server Process
id: 9d4f1e3b-c1c4-4f8a-bb18-7b2d2c5e8a13
description: Detects PHP/PHAR/PHTML files written into upload-style paths by a web-server process — the post-bypass artifact of CVE-2026-48062 where CodeIgniter4 ext_in trusted MIME-derived extension over filename.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx
  - https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.t1036.008
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\httpd.exe'
      - '\nginx.exe'
      - '\php-cgi.exe'
      - '\caddy.exe'
  selection_ext:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.php'
      - '.phtml'
      - '.phar'
      - '.php5'
      - '.php7'
      - '.pht'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\uploads\'
      - '\public\'
      - '\writable\'
      - '\avatar'
  condition: all of selection_*
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) @EventID:11 @Image:(*\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE OR *\httpd.exe OR *\nginx.exe OR *\php-cgi.exe OR *\php-fpm) @TargetFilename:(*\uploads\*.php OR */uploads/*.php OR *\writable\*.php OR */writable/*.php OR *\public\*.phtml OR */public/*.phtml OR *\avatar*.php OR */avatar*.php)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten ContextImageFileName=/(w3wp|httpd|nginx|php-cgi|php-fpm|caddy)\.exe$/i TargetFileName=/\.(php[3457]?|phtml|phar|pht|inc)$/i | regex("(?i)(\\\\|/)(uploads?|public|writable|avatar|images?|media|assets)(\\\\|/)", field=TargetFileName) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action=created (Filesystem.file_name="*.php" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phtml" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phar" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.php5" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.php7") (Filesystem.file_path="*\\uploads\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/uploads/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\public\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/public/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\writable\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/writable/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\avatar*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/avatar*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where process_name IN ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-fpm","php-cgi.exe")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action=created (Filesystem.file_name="*.php" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phtml" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phar" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.php5" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.php7") (Filesystem.file_path="*\\uploads\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/uploads/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\public\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/public/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\writable\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/writable/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\avatar*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/avatar*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where process_name IN ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-fpm","php-cgi.exe")
HTTP GET to PHP file inside /uploads path (CodeIgniter4 webshell invocation) AIExploitation High
Detects HTTP requests resolving to a PHP file under an upload/avatar directory served by the web tier. Legitimate apps serve only images from /uploads; a 200-OK GET on /uploads/*.php is the unmistakable post-bypass execution of the CVE-2026-48062 dropped shell. Rationale: Article precondition: 'store uploads in a web-accessible directory ... allow PHP or other executable files to run from that directory ... may lead to arbitrary code execution'. A successful GET/POST to /uploads/*.php returning 2xx is the literal execution event the article warns about. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://codeigniter.com/user_guide/libraries/uploaded_files.html#moving-files
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legacy app deliberately serving PHP entry-points from /uploads (rare but exists)
  • Penetration-test simulation hitting /uploads/test.php intentionally
  • WordPress plugin/theme installers that put admin PHP under public dirs and call them
  • Misconfigured CI deploy that places router.php in an uploads-named directory
Suppression filter
| where csUriStem !has_any ("/uploads/index.php", "/uploads/router.php", "/uploads/test.php")
| where cIP !in ("<authorized-pentest-IPs>")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the exact URL, response size, csUserAgent, and prior 100 requests from the same cIP — webshells typically have low response sizes and repeated probes (id, whoami, ls). Step 2 (contain): Block the cIP at WAF, isolate the affected web host, kill all w3wp/nginx/php-fpm child processes spawned in the last hour, and quarantine the .php file under /uploads. Begin forensic capture. Step 3 (hunt): Cross-correlate with DeviceProcessEvents on the same DeviceName for cmd/powershell/sh children of the web-server process; sweep all webroots for new .php files in upload-style paths; check outbound DNS/IP from the web account for C2 beacons; verify CodeIgniter4 version is >= 4.7.3 on every instance.
// Inbound HTTP request paths are not natively in Defender XDR — pivot on the web-server process spawning shells from its CWD
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe", "httpd.exe", "nginx.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "php-fpm")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("\\uploads\\", "/uploads/", "\\avatar", "/avatar", "\\writable\\", "/writable/")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/uploads/", "\\uploads\\", ".php")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "sh", "bash", "dash", "whoami.exe", "net.exe", "ipconfig.exe", "ifconfig", "id", "uname")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod in ("GET", "POST", "HEAD")
| where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)/(uploads?|avatar|writable|public/uploads?|public/avatar|media|images?)/[^/]+\.(php[3457]?|phtml|phar|pht)$"
| where scStatus in (200, 201, 202, 301, 302)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, scStatus, csUserAgent, csUserName, TimeTaken
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: HTTP Request to PHP File Inside Upload/Avatar Path
id: f3a5e1d2-2b1f-4a9c-8e7d-1c4a2b9f6e0a
description: HTTP request reaching a .php file under an upload-style path — strong post-exploitation signal for CVE-2026-48062 CodeIgniter4 ext_in bypass where a polyglot shell.php was dropped and invoked.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.t1190
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection:
    cs-uri-stem|re: '(?i)/(uploads?|avatar|writable|public/uploads?|media)/[^/]+\.(php[3457]?|phtml|phar|pht)$'
  filter_status:
    sc-status:
      - 200
      - 201
      - 301
      - 302
  condition: selection and filter_status
level: high
source:(nginx OR apache OR iis OR cloudfront OR azure.activity_logs) (@http.url_details.path:*/uploads/*.php OR @http.url_details.path:*/uploads/*.phtml OR @http.url_details.path:*/uploads/*.phar OR @http.url_details.path:*/avatar*/*.php OR @http.url_details.path:*/writable/*.php OR @http.url_details.path:*/public/uploads/*.php) @http.status_code:[200 TO 399]
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(w3wp|httpd|nginx|php-cgi|php-fpm)\.exe$/i | regex("(?i)(\\\\|/)(uploads?|avatar|writable|public)(\\\\|/)", field=ParentImageFileName) | ImageFileName=/(cmd|powershell|pwsh|sh|bash|whoami|net|ipconfig|id|uname)(\.exe)?$/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentImageFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.http_user_agent) as agents values(Web.http_method) as methods from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*/uploads/*.php*" OR Web.url="*/avatar*/*.php*" OR Web.url="*/writable/*.php*" OR Web.url="*/public/uploads/*.php*") Web.status=200 by Web.src Web.dest Web.url | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.http_user_agent) as agents values(Web.http_method) as methods from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*/uploads/*.php*" OR Web.url="*/avatar*/*.php*" OR Web.url="*/writable/*.php*" OR Web.url="*/public/uploads/*.php*") Web.status=200 by Web.src Web.dest Web.url | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
Upload immediately followed by web-server shell execution (CVE-2026-48062 RCE chain) AIExploitation High
Correlates a fresh .php/.phtml/.phar file written into a public webroot by a web-server process with that same process spawning a shell or recon binary within 30 seconds. This is the exact 'upload then invoke' chain the article describes; the temporal join eliminates standalone false positives from either signal alone. Rationale: Article workflow: 'shell.php containing GIF-like content could pass validation ... save uploaded files using the original client filename ... store uploads in a web-accessible directory ... allow PHP or other executable files to run from that directory'. The temporal correlation (write-then-exec within 30s) is the high-fidelity RCE shape; either event alone is ambiguous, the join is not. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/File_Upload_Cheat_Sheet.html
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • CMS plugin self-install writing a PHP file then immediately reloading the app and spawning helper processes
  • CI/CD deploy that drops .php into public path and runs a post-deploy shell hook
  • Composer/artisan executions invoked through web UI that legitimately write+exec
  • Auto-installer/setup wizard that writes a config.php and runs initial migration commands
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("composer", "artisan migrate", "wp-cli", "deploy.sh")
| where ShellCmd !has_any ("--health-check", "--version")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the FileSHA256 and review the polyglot signature (image magic + <?php). Pull the shell ProcessCommandLine and any subsequent process tree. Identify the source IP of the upload from W3CIISLog within ±10s of FileTime. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host, quarantine the file by hash, kill the spawned shell/process tree, block the source IP, and patch CodeIgniter4 to >= 4.7.3 immediately. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep the estate for the same SHA256 hash; pivot on the source IP across all webservers and CommonSecurityLog for 30 days; check outbound DNS/network from the web-server account for unfamiliar destinations; review any access keys/credentials reachable from the web tier and rotate them.
let WindowSeconds = 30;
let UploadDrops = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe", "httpd.exe", "nginx.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "php-fpm", "caddy.exe")
    | where FileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php[3457]?|phtml|phar|pht)$"
    | where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)(\\|/)(uploads?|public|writable|avatar|media)(\\|/)"
    | project FileTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, FileSHA256 = SHA256,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessId;
let ShellSpawns = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe", "httpd.exe", "nginx.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "php-fpm", "caddy.exe")
    | where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "sh", "bash", "dash", "whoami.exe", "net.exe", "ipconfig.exe", "ifconfig", "id", "uname", "hostname.exe")
    | project ProcTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, ShellFile = FileName, ShellCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessId;
UploadDrops
| join kind=inner ShellSpawns on DeviceId
| where ProcTime between (FileTime .. FileTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', ProcTime, FileTime)
| project FileTime, ProcTime, DelaySec, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, ShellFile, ShellCmd
| order by FileTime desc
let WindowSeconds = 30;
let UploadDrops = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
    | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(w3wp|httpd|nginx|php-cgi|php-fpm|caddy)(\.exe)?$"
    | where TargetFileExtension in~ ("php", "phtml", "phar", "php5", "php7", "pht")
    | where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)(\\|/)(uploads?|public|writable|avatar|media)(\\|/)"
    | project FileTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessId;
let ShellSpawns = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(w3wp|httpd|nginx|php-cgi|php-fpm|caddy)(\.exe)?$"
    | where TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(cmd|powershell|pwsh|sh|bash|dash|whoami|net|ipconfig|ifconfig|id|uname|hostname)(\.exe)?$"
    | project ProcTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName;
UploadDrops
| join kind=inner ShellSpawns on DvcHostname
| where ProcTime between (FileTime .. FileTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', ProcTime, FileTime)
| project FileTime, ProcTime, DelaySec, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256,
          ParentProcessName, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by FileTime desc
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(w3wp|httpd|nginx|php-cgi|php-fpm|caddy)\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/(cmd|powershell|pwsh|sh|bash|whoami|net|ipconfig|id|uname|hostname)(\.exe)?$/i | join({#event_simpleName=FileWritten ContextImageFileName=/(w3wp|httpd|nginx|php-cgi|php-fpm|caddy)\.exe$/i TargetFileName=/(?i)(\\\\|/)(uploads?|public|writable|avatar|media)(\\\\|/).*\.(php[3457]?|phtml|phar|pht)$/}, field=aid, include=[TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName]) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentImageFileName, ImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action=created (Filesystem.file_name="*.php" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phtml" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phar") (Filesystem.file_path="*\\uploads\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/uploads/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\public\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/public/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\writable\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/writable/*") by _time Filesystem.dest Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | rename _time as fileTime | join type=inner dest [| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-fpm") Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","whoami.exe","net.exe","ipconfig.exe","id","uname") by _time Processes.dest Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename _time as procTime] | where procTime >= fileTime AND procTime <= (fileTime + 30) | table fileTime procTime dest file_path file_name process_name parent_process_name process
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action=created (Filesystem.file_name="*.php" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phtml" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phar") (Filesystem.file_path="*\\uploads\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/uploads/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\public\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/public/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\writable\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/writable/*") by _time Filesystem.dest Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | rename _time as fileTime | join type=inner dest [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-fpm") Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","whoami.exe","net.exe","ipconfig.exe","id","uname") by _time Processes.dest Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename _time as procTime] | where procTime >= fileTime AND procTime <= (fileTime + 30) | table fileTime procTime dest file_path file_name process_name parent_process_name process
Multipart upload: filename extension mismatches declared Content-Type (ext_in bypass attempt) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts WAF / reverse-proxy traffic for multipart/form-data POSTs where the part's filename ends in an executable extension (.php/.phtml/.phar) while its Content-Type header claims to be an image. This is the precise wire-shape an attacker uses to exploit CVE-2026-48062's ext_in flaw. Rationale: Article literally documents the bypass: 'uploaded[avatar]|is_image[avatar]|mime_in[avatar,image/gif]|ext_in[avatar,gif] ... a file named shell.php containing GIF-like content could pass validation'. The wire fingerprint is multipart Content-Type=image/* with filename=*.php — anything matching is either the exploit or a misconfigured tool. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://codeigniter.com/user_guide/libraries/validation.html#rules-for-file-uploads
ATT&CKT1190 T1036.008
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Misconfigured upload tools that mis-declare Content-Type
  • Security scanners (Burp, ZAP, sqlmap) testing upload endpoints with mismatched MIME/extension
  • Developer testing the patch via crafted POST
  • Threat-intel honeypot probes against the exposed endpoint
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in ("<authorized-pentest-IPs>", "<internal-QA-IPs>")
| where RequestClientApplication !has_any ("sqlmap", "Burp", "ZAP")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full multipart body, decode the file content's first bytes — confirm whether it's a real polyglot (image magic + PHP) or a benign mistake. Check SourceIP reputation. Step 2 (contain): If confirmed exploit, block the SourceIP at WAF, quarantine any file saved server-side, isolate the affected host, and upgrade CodeIgniter4 to >= 4.7.3. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep WAF logs for any other multipart POSTs from the same SourceIP across last 30d; pull DeviceFileEvents on the receiving host for new .php in webroot; pivot on the User-Agent across the estate.
// Multipart-body inspection is a WAF-layer capability; Defender XDR does not parse request bodies. Pivot via DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound proxy traffic from suspected upload tools.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or SHA1 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or MD5 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or SHA1 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or MD5 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Bun runtime fetched mid-npm-install (Shai-Hulud / Mini Shai-Hulud staging) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Nx s1ngularity 'telemetry.js' postinstall payload execution · [LLM] Implicit node-gyp rebuild from binding.gyp during npm install · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — npm v12 delivers one of the biggest security improvements in years
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Shai-Hulud Webhook.site C2 beacon from Node/npm/Bun process · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] TruffleHog secret scanner spawned by Node/npm (Shai-Hulud worm pattern) · [LLM] Nx s1ngularity exfil: GitHub repo 's1ngularity-repository' / 'results.b64' · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Nx s1ngularity 'telemetry.js' postinstall payload execution AIExploitation High
Detects execution of the telemetry.js postinstall script associated with the Nx s1ngularity npm supply-chain compromise (Aug 2025). The script is invoked by npm during install, scrapes GitHub/npm tokens, SSH keys and crypto wallets, and exfiltrates them to attacker-created public GitHub repos. Rationale: Anchored on the article-named 'telemetry.js' postinstall script and 's1ngularity' brand string. Cross-checked at the Nx post-mortem (nx.dev/blog/s1ngularity-postmortem) and Datadog Security Labs which both confirm telemetry.js as the canonical Nx-poisoned filename invoked from package.json's postinstall hook. Parent-filename narrowing to JS package managers removes the obvious FP shape. Cross-checked against: • https://nx.dev/blog/s1ngularity-postmortem • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/learnings-from-recent-npm-compromises/ • https://snyk.io/blog/weaponizing-ai-coding-agents-for-malware-in-the-nx-malicious-package/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Nx packages published before/after the malicious window — current versions of @nx/* may still ship a benign telemetry.js
  • Developer hand-running 'node scripts/telemetry.js' in a non-Nx repo unrelated to npm install
  • Internal monorepo with a homegrown telemetry.js used in pre/post hooks
  • CI runners that pin to a known-clean Nx version but still surface the filename
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has "telemetry.js" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("\\node_modules\\@nrwl\\nx\\","\\node_modules\\nx\\") and SHA256 in ("<known-good-nx-sha256>"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: pull the full ProcessCreate row + parent cmdline; confirm the parent is an active 'npm install' or 'yarn add' invocation and not a manual 'node telemetry.js' run. Pivot DeviceFileEvents for SHA256 of the telemetry.js file under node_modules. 2) CONTAIN: isolate the device via Defender Live Response, revoke the user's GitHub PAT, npm token, and any AWS keys from ~/.aws/credentials, and rotate SSH keys touched on that host. 3) HUNT: search for outbound connections to api.github.com creating 's1ngularity-repository*' under the user's GH account, query DeviceFileEvents for 'results.b64' across the fleet, and review npm audit log for which package version dragged it in.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","bun.exe")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "telemetry.js" or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("s1ngularity","@nrwl/nx","nx-cloud")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd","bun.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "telemetry.js" or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("s1ngularity","@nrwl/nx","nx-cloud")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Nx s1ngularity telemetry.js postinstall malware execution
id: 2f8e4b3c-1d6e-4a7c-9e8f-3b2c1a9d8e7f
description: Detects execution of telemetry.js as a child of npm/node/yarn/pnpm/bun, the postinstall payload used in the Nx s1ngularity supply-chain attack
references:

    - https://nx.dev/blog/s1ngularity-postmortem

author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:

source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE OR *\\npm.exe OR *\\NPM.EXE OR *\\npm.cmd OR *\\NPM.CMD OR *\\yarn.cmd OR *\\pnpm.cmd OR *\\bun.exe) @CommandLine:(*telemetry.js* OR *s1ngularity*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(node\.exe|npm\.(cmd|exe)|npx\.cmd|yarn\.(cmd|exe)|pnpm\.(cmd|exe)|bun\.exe)$/i CommandLine=/telemetry\.js|s1ngularity/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

TruffleHog secret scanner spawned by Node/npm (Shai-Hulud worm pattern) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the TruffleHog secret-scanning binary being launched as a child of node/npm/yarn/pnpm/bun. The Shai-Hulud worm installs the Bun runtime mid-install and uses TruffleHog to scrape API keys, tokens, and cloud credentials from the host before pushing them to a hardcoded webhook. Rationale: Article explicitly names TruffleHog as the Shai-Hulud credential-harvest tool. Sysdig and ReversingLabs both confirm trufflehog is fetched + executed under npm install context. Pairing the binary signal with a JS-package-manager parent eliminates the legit dev/CI TruffleHog runs (which are launched from CI YAML or the user shell, not from node). Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages • https://www.reversinglabs.com/blog/shai-hulud-worm-npm • https://checkmarx.com/zero-post/inside-shai-huluds-maw-how-the-npm-worm-exploits-and-propagates/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Pre-commit hook calling 'npx trufflehog' as legitimate secret scanning (common in modern dev workflows)
  • GitHub Actions self-hosted runner with the trufflehog action where the workflow shell parent is node
  • CI orchestrator that wraps trufflehog in a node-based runner like 'turbo run'
  • Security researcher hand-running 'npx trufflehog filesystem .' against a repo
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("pre-commit","husky","lint-staged") or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("git-secrets","pre-commit"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: pull TruffleHog cmdline — Shai-Hulud invokes with '--json' and filesystem/git scopes targeting $HOME and common cred dirs. Check whether the parent chain includes an in-flight 'npm install' / 'npm ci' (vs an explicit user-typed npx). Sample the calling node process's argv. 2) CONTAIN: isolate the host, revoke all GitHub/npm/AWS/GCP tokens held by the user, and rotate any SSH keys present. Pull node_modules/<suspect-package> for IR. 3) HUNT: search for outbound to webhook.site (see Shai-Hulud beacon UC), look for new public GitHub repos under the user's account, query DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound to bun.sh and github.com/oven-sh/bun, and pivot on the SHA256 of the trufflehog binary across the fleet.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName has "trufflehog" or ProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","bun.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd","bun.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has "trufflehog" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd","bun.exe","sh","bash")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Nx s1ngularity exfil: GitHub repo 's1ngularity-repository' / 'results.b64' AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the Nx s1ngularity exfiltration pattern where the postinstall payload creates a public GitHub repository (s1ngularity-repository, sometimes numerically suffixed) under the victim's own account and commits a triple-base64-encoded credential bundle named results.b64. Surfaced via gh CLI, git, curl, or wget commandlines. Rationale: Anchored on two literal Nx s1ngularity strings ('s1ngularity-repository' and 'results.b64') corroborated by the Nx post-mortem, Datadog Security Labs, and CyberSecureFox. These strings are essentially unique — neither has a benign use. Multi-source detection (process + file) catches both the gh/git invocation and the staged bundle file. Cross-checked against: • https://nx.dev/blog/s1ngularity-postmortem • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/learnings-from-recent-npm-compromises/ • https://cybersecurefox.com/en/nx-supply-chain-attack-s1ngularity-github-actions-npm/
ATT&CKT1567.001 T1567
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal red-team replicating the IR scenario in a lab
  • Security researcher cloning the public s1ngularity-response repo (BunsDev/s1ngularity-response) for analysis — git clone URL would mention it
  • Threat-intel feed enrichment script that posts the literal string in a benign context
  • Incident response document containing the IOC strings opened in a script editor
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: capture the full cmdline + parent chain. Identify which GitHub account was authenticated via 'gh auth status' on the host. List public repos under that account ('gh repo list --visibility public') and check for s1ngularity-repository, s1ngularity-repository-0, ...-1, etc. 2) CONTAIN: delete the attacker-created public repos immediately (they expose credentials publicly). Revoke the GitHub PAT and all OAuth grants on that account, rotate npm/AWS/GCP keys, force-rotate SSH keypairs. Isolate the host. 3) HUNT: pivot on the user's other endpoints, search EmailEvents for any phishing that compromised the GitHub credential, and check DeviceFileEvents for ~/.gitconfig / ~/.npmrc tampering. Block 's1ngularity-repository*' as a regex in egress DLP.
union
(
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)

Shai-Hulud Webhook.site C2 beacon from Node/npm/Bun process AICommand & Control High
Detects outbound traffic to webhook.site, and specifically to the Shai-Hulud-attributed bundle path bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7, originating from a node/npm/yarn/pnpm/bun-spawned process. webhook.site is a free request-bin service that Shai-Hulud hardcodes as its credential dropbox. Rationale: webhook.site is a confirmed hardcoded Shai-Hulud C2 endpoint per Sysdig and Checkmarx (the bb8ca5f6 token is the literal bundle ID published in their write-ups). Tagging only npm-ecosystem-spawned connections cuts the legitimate developer-testing FP volume. The ShaiHuludMarker column lets the SOC promote any hit with the literal bundle ID straight to incident. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages • https://checkmarx.com/zero-post/inside-shai-huluds-maw-how-the-npm-worm-exploits-and-propagates/ • https://www.reversinglabs.com/blog/shai-hulud-worm-npm
ATT&CKT1567 T1071.001 T1102
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer testing a Stripe/Twilio/Slack webhook by curling webhook.site from a node script during local dev
  • CI pipeline using webhook.site as a request bin for integration tests
  • Postman or Insomnia desktop client (electron/node-based) hitting webhook.site
  • QA engineer running 'npm test' against a service that sends webhooks for verification
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("test","integration","e2e","jest","mocha","playwright") and not (RemoteUrl has "bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: confirm whether the URL path contains 'bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7' (ShaiHuludMarker=TRUE = treat as confirmed). For non-marker hits, pull the parent npm install context — was a package being installed when the connection fired? 2) CONTAIN: isolate host, block webhook.site at the proxy/DNS for npm-ecosystem User-Agents, force-revoke all GitHub PAT / npm tokens / cloud creds on the host. 3) HUNT: hash any node_modules subdir modified in the prior 24h, search for TruffleHog spawn (see related UC), look for s1ngularity-repository creation, and pivot on the SHA256 of the bun binary if present. Add the bb8ca5f6 path to TI feed and the DLP egress block list.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "webhook.site"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","bun.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd","bun.exe")
| extend ShaiHuludMarker = iff(RemoteUrl has "bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7", "TRUE", "FALSE")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName,
          AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          RemoteUrl, ShaiHuludMarker, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by ShaiHuludMarker desc, Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(
    ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstHostname has "webhook.site" or Url has "webhook.site"
    | extend ShaiHuludMarker = iff(Url has "bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7", "TRUE", "FALSE")
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="NetworkSession", Host=DvcHostname, SrcUser=SrcUsername, Dst=DstHostname, Url, ShaiHuludMarker
),
(
    DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name =~ "webhook.site" or Name endswith ".webhook.site"
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="DNS", Host=Computer, SrcUser="", Dst=Name, Url="", ShaiHuludMarker="DNS-only"
)
| order by ShaiHuludMarker desc, TimeGenerated desc

Bun runtime fetched mid-npm-install (Shai-Hulud / Mini Shai-Hulud staging) AIDelivery Medium
Detects npm/node/yarn/pnpm pulling and installing the Bun JavaScript runtime during a package install. Both Shai-Hulud (Nov 2025) and Mini Shai-Hulud (May 2026) stage the cred-stealer payload inside Bun, so an npm install that drags in Bun on a host that previously never ran it is a strong supply-chain marker. Rationale: Article explicitly says Shai-Hulud 'installed the Bun runtime during setup' and Mini Shai-Hulud 'planted a preinstall hook that pulled the Bun runtime'. The two URL signals (bun.sh/install and github.com/oven-sh/bun) are how Bun's documented installer fetches. Pairing with a node/npm parent eliminates the legitimate dev-who-runs-curl-from-shell FP. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/
ATT&CKT1105 T1195.002 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer or CI runner that genuinely uses Bun as a runtime and runs the official installer from a node-wrapped task
  • Devcontainer post-create script that node-bootstraps Bun on container build
  • Polyglot monorepo where one workspace runs 'npm run setup' that contains 'curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash'
  • Engineer evaluating Bun as a replacement runtime and triggering installer from a node script
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName in (dynamic(["<known-bun-dev-hosts>"])) or AccountName in (dynamic(["<known-bun-developers>"])))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: was Bun already present on this host before this event? Query DeviceInfo / DeviceFileEvents for prior bun.exe sightings on this DeviceId. If first-seen on host AND during an npm install, treat as suspect. 2) CONTAIN: stop the npm install, isolate the host, pull node_modules for IR snapshot. Revoke tokens the host had access to. 3) HUNT: check the same time window for TruffleHog spawn, webhook.site beacons, and s1ngularity-repository creation under the user's GitHub. Pivot per-host: a new bun.exe SHA256 appearing on N hosts within hours = worm propagation.
let JsPkgMgr = dynamic(["node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe"]);
let BunSignals = dynamic(["bun.sh/install","oven-sh/bun","install.sh"]);
union
(
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (JsPkgMgr)
        or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (JsPkgMgr)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (BunSignals) or FileName in~ ("bun.exe","bun")
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              Source = "Process",
              Evidence = strcat(FileName, " :: ", ProcessCommandLine),
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
),
(
    DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any ("bun.sh/install","oven-sh/bun")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (JsPkgMgr) or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
        or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (JsPkgMgr)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName,
              AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              Source = "Network",
              Evidence = RemoteUrl,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
)
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("bun.sh/install","oven-sh/bun")
    or (ActingProcessCommandLine has "curl" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "install.sh" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "bun")
    or ActingProcessName endswith "bun.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Implicit node-gyp rebuild from binding.gyp during npm install AIExploitation Medium
Hunt-tier surface for the binding.gyp attack path that npm v12 closes — packages that ship a binding.gyp trigger an implicit 'node-gyp rebuild' during npm install with no script declared in package.json, executing arbitrary build code. Hunt for node-gyp invocations spawned by npm/yarn/pnpm and baseline against your approved native-module set. Rationale: The article calls out the binding.gyp attack vector explicitly: 'When a package ships a binding.gyp, npm runs an implicit node-gyp rebuild for it during install, so a dependency with a spotless package.json can still execute code just by carrying that one build file.' Aikido's own research is the second-source citation in the article. Hunting tier — node-gyp is benign for many native modules (sqlite3, sharp, bcrypt). The aggregation surfaces which native module a host is compiling so the SOC can baseline. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/npm-v12-block-postinstall
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059 T1027.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate native modules: sqlite3, better-sqlite3, sharp, bcrypt, canvas, node-sass, node-saml, node-pty — all use binding.gyp
  • CI builder building any Electron app from source
  • Native-module rebuild after a Node major version bump (common across the fleet at once)
  • Local 'npm install' on a developer laptop pulling in any C/C++-bound package
Suppression filter
| where NativeModule !in ("sqlite3","better-sqlite3","sharp","bcrypt","canvas","node-sass","sass","node-pty","node-saml","node-expat","deasync","fsevents","keytar","node-gyp","nodegit","grpc","@grpc/grpc-js")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: pull NativeModule from the aggregation. If it's in your known-good native-module allowlist (sqlite3, sharp, etc.) — close. If it's an unfamiliar package name, pivot npm registry view of that package and check publish date / maintainer change history. 2) CONTAIN: only escalate if the package is unknown — quarantine the host, snapshot the node_modules/<module>/build/ artifacts. 3) HUNT: pull the module's binding.gyp from disk and inspect 'actions' / 'sources' fields for shellouts. Search the fleet for that module name across DeviceProcessEvents to scope. Cross-ref against npm v12 readiness output ('npm approve-scripts --allow-scripts-pending').
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (ProcessCommandLine has "node-gyp" and ProcessCommandLine has "rebuild")
    or ProcessCommandLine has "binding.gyp"
    or FileName in~ ("node-gyp.cmd","node-gyp.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","bun.exe")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| extend NativeModule = extract(@"node_modules[\\/]+([^\\/]+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            Hits = count(),
            DistinctModules = dcount(NativeModule),
            SampleModules = make_set(NativeModule, 25),
            SampleCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine)
            by DeviceName, AccountName
| order by FirstSeen desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (CommandLine has "node-gyp" and CommandLine has "rebuild")
    or CommandLine has "binding.gyp"
    or NewProcessName has_any ("node-gyp.cmd","node-gyp.exe")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd","bun.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| extend NativeModule = extract(@"node_modules[\\/]+([^\\/]+)", 1, CommandLine)
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Hits = count(),
            DistinctModules = dcount(NativeModule),
            SampleModules = make_set(NativeModule, 25),
            SampleCmd = any(CommandLine)
            by Computer, Account
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE OR *\\npm.exe OR *\\NPM.EXE OR *\\npm.cmd OR *\\yarn.cmd OR *\\pnpm.cmd OR *\\bun.exe) (@CommandLine:*node-gyp* OR @CommandLine:*binding.gyp*)

| regex("node_modules[\\\\/]+(?<native_module>[^\\\\/]+)", field=CommandLine)
